verdict.rationale: Trivy's docs state that it scans container images and filesystems (non-git sources) for exposed secrets, with secret scanning on by default, and that it can also scan image configuration for secrets. That covers the Docker-image part of the story. Nothing in the evidence shows scanning of S3 buckets or CI logs, so only part of the story is delivered. Missing for 10: S3 bucket secret scanning, CI log secret scanning, independent hands-on corroboration of secret detection.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can scan non-git sources like S3 buckets, Docker images, and CI logs for leaked secrets

citations.quote: Trivy scans any container image, filesystem and git repository to detect exposed secrets like passwords, api keys, and tokens. Secret scanning is enabled by default.
Trivy scans the configuration of container images for * Misconfigurations * Secrets
